title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 120 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 590–592 (Night 120, continuing directly from nights-119), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 120 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. ʿAzīz goes on with his tale to Tāj al-Mulūk. His cousin ʿAzīza is buried, and his mother tells him that with her last breath ʿAzīza forgave him, left him a pair of sayings to speak whenever he leaves his beloved — “faithfulness is fair, and treachery is foul” — and left a keepsake that the mother will give him only when she sees him mourn. When he repeats the sayings to the lady, she blesses the dead girl, confesses that she had meant him harm and that ʿAzīza’s words have saved him, and warns him, now that his cousin is gone, to keep away from every woman of her kind. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْمُوفِيَةُ لِلْعِشْرِينَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-mūfiyatu li-al-ʿishrīna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the completing for the twenty after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and twentieth night,
sentences.n: al-mūfiya li-al-ʿishrīn, “the one completing the twenty”: the print names a round-numbered night this way, as it did the sixtieth and the hundredth.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِى أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الشَّابَّ عَزِيزْ قَالَ لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ ثُمَّ دَخَلْتُ الدَّارَ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي أُمِّي قَالَتْ إِنَّ خَطِيئَتَهَا فِي ذِمَّتِكَ فَلَا سَامَحَكَ اللَّهُ مِنْ دَمِهَا تَبًّا لَكَ مِنِ ابْنِ عَمٍّ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-shābba ʿAzīz qāla li-tāji al-mulūki thumma dakhaltu al-dāra fa-lammā raʾatnī ummī qālat inna khaṭīʾatahā fī dhimmatika fa-lā sāmaḥaka allāhu min damihā tabban laka min ibni ʿammin
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the youth ʿAzīz said to Tāj al-Mulūk: Then I entered the house, and when my mother saw me she said: The sin of her (is) in your charge; so may God not pardon you of her blood. Ruin to you, of a cousin!
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the young man ʿAzīz said to Tāj al-Mulūk: Then I went into the house, and when my mother saw me she said, “The guilt of her death is on your conscience; may God never forgive you her blood! A curse on you, for a cousin!”
sentences.n: The print has خطيئها, a misprint for خطيئتها (khaṭīʾatahā, “her sin”, that is, the sin of her death), corrected here; the same word comes back correctly at the end of the night before and later in this one. The night opens by going back over the last lines of the night before. The name ʿAzīz stands without the accusative alif its place after al-shābba would call for, and is read here without a case ending. tabban laka, “ruin to you”: an old curse. min ibni ʿammin, “of a cousin”: min here names what kind of thing he is, “what a cousin you are!”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ أَبِي جَاءَ وَجَهَّزْنَاهَا وَأَخْرَجْنَاهَا وَشَيَّعْنَا جِنَازَتَهَا وَدَفَنَّاهَا وَعَمِلْنَا عَلَي قَبْرِهَا الْخَتَمَاتِ وَمَكَثْنَا عَلَى الْقَبْرِ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ رَجَعْنَا وَدَخَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ وَأَنَا حَزِينٌ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna abī jāʾa wa-jahhaznāhā wa-akhrajnāhā wa-shayyaʿnā jināzatahā wa-dafannāhā wa-ʿamilnā ʿalā qabrihā al-khatamāti wa-makathnā ʿalā al-qabri thalāthata ayyāmin thumma rajaʿnā wa-dakhalnā al-bayta wa-anā ḥazīnun ʿalayhā
sentences.l: Then my father came, and we prepared-her and brought-her-out and escorted her bier and buried-her, and we made over her grave the complete-recitations; and we stayed at the grave three days; then we returned and entered the house, and I (was) grieving over her.
sentences.i: Then my father came, and we made her ready for burial, carried her out, followed her bier and buried her, and had the whole Qurʾān recited over her grave. We stayed at the grave three days; then we came back and went into the house, and I was grieving for her.
sentences.n: jahhaza, “make ready”: of the dead, to wash and shroud the body. al-khatamāt, plural of khatma, a reading of the whole Qurʾān from beginning to end, here recited over the grave for the dead. The print spells ʿalā “over” with a dotted yāʾ (علي); it is read ʿalā. thalātha is written with a dagger alif, as the print has it.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيَّ أُمِّي وَقَالَتْ لِي إِنَّ قَصْدِي أَنْ أَعْرِفَ مَا كُنْتَ تَفْعَلُهُ مَعَهَا حَتَّى فَقَعْتَ مَرَارَتَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-aqbalat ʿalayya ummī wa-qālat lī inna qaṣdī an aʿrifa mā kunta tafʿaluhu maʿahā ḥattā faqaʿta marāratahā
sentences.l: And my mother came-up to me and said to me: My aim (is) that I know what you used to do with her, until you burst her gall-bladder.
sentences.i: My mother came to me and said, “What I want is to know what you were doing to her, that you broke her heart.
sentences.n: faqaʿta marāratahā, “you burst her gall-bladder”: to die of grief or rage, in the old physiology; English would say “broke her heart”. The fatḥa on كنتَ and فقعتَ is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَإِنِّي يَا وَلَدِي كُنْتُ أَسْأَلُ مِنْهَا فِي كُلِّ الْأَوْقَاتِ عَنْ سَبَبِ مَرَضِهَا فَمَا أَطْلَعَتْنِي عَلَى شَيْءٍ وَلَمْ تُخْبِرْنِي بِهِ فَبِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ أَخْبِرْنِي عَمَّا كُنْتَ تَفْعَلُ مَعَهَا حَتَّى مَاتَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-innī yā waladī kuntu asʾalu minhā fī kulli al-awqāti ʿan sababi maraḍihā fa-mā aṭlaʿatnī ʿalā shayʾin wa-lam tukhbirnī bihi fa-bi-allāhi ʿalayka akhbirnī ʿammā kunta tafʿalu maʿahā ḥattā mātat
sentences.l: And I, O my son, used to ask of her at all the times about the cause of her illness, and she did not let-me-see upon a thing and did not inform me of it. So by God upon you, inform me about what you used to do with her until she died.
sentences.i: And I, my son, asked her again and again what was the cause of her illness, but she let me see nothing and told me nothing of it. So I beg you by God, tell me what you were doing to her, that she died.”
sentences.n: saʾala min, “ask of” someone: a spoken use; Classical says saʾalahā. aṭlaʿa ʿalā, “let (someone) see, acquaint with”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. fa-bi-allāhi ʿalayka, “by God upon you”: bi- is the bi- of oaths, “by”; the whole is a plea, “I beg you by God”. ʿammā is ʿan mā, “about what”.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ مَا عَمِلْتُ شَيْأً فَقَالَتِ اللَّهُ يَقْتَصُّ لَهَا مِنْكَ فَإِنَّهَا مَا ذَكَرَتْ لِي شَيْأً بَلْ كَتَمَتْ أَمْرَهَا حَتَّى مَاتَتْ وَهِيَ رَاضِيَةٌ عَنْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu mā ʿamiltu shayʾan fa-qālati allāhu yaqtaṣṣu lahā minka fa-innahā mā dhakarat lī shayʾan bal katamat amrahā ḥattā mātat wa-hiya rāḍiyatun ʿanka
sentences.l: And I said: I did not do a thing. And she said: God (will) take-retribution for her from you; for she did not mention to me a thing, but she hid her affair until she died, and she (was) content with you.
sentences.i: I said, “I did nothing.” She said, “God will take revenge on you for her! She never said a word to me; she kept her secret until she died, and she died at peace with you.”
sentences.n: The print has ثيأ, a misprint for شيأ, “a thing”, corrected here; the first شيأ in the sentence is printed correctly. The print spells shayʾan with the hamza on an alif, شيأ, as it often does (it also writes شيء, as in the sentence before). iqtaṣṣa li- … min, “take retribution for (someone) from (someone)”: li- is “on behalf of”, min “from”, the guilty one. rāḍiyatun ʿan, “content with, at peace with”.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا مَاتَتْ كُنْتُ عِنْدَهَا فَفَتَحَتْ عَيْنَهَا وَقَالَتْ لِي يَا امْرَأَةَ عَمِّي جَعَلَ اللَّهُ وَلَدَكِ فِي حِلٍّ مِنْ دَمِي وَلَا آخَذَهُ بِمَا فَعَلَ مَعِي وَإِنَّمَا نَقَلَنِى اللَّهُ مِنَ الدَّارِ الدُّنْيَا الْفَانِيَةِ إِلَى الدَّارِ آلْآخِرَةِ الْبَاقِيَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā mātat kuntu ʿindahā fa-fataḥat ʿaynahā wa-qālat lī yā imraʾata ʿammī jaʿala allāhu waladaki fī ḥillin min damī wa-lā ākhadhahu bi-mā faʿala maʿī wa-innamā naqalanī allāhu mina al-dāri al-dunyā al-fāniyati ilā al-dāri al-ākhirati al-bāqiyati
sentences.l: And when she died I was with her, and she opened her eye and said to me: O wife of my uncle, may God make your son in release from my blood, and may He not take-him-to-task for what he did with me; it is only that God (has) moved me from the abode the nearer, the perishing, to the abode the last, the abiding.
sentences.i: “When she was dying I was with her. She opened her eyes and said to me, ‘O my aunt, may God hold your son free of my blood, and not call him to account for what he did to me. God is only taking me from the house of this passing world to the house of the world to come, which lasts.’
sentences.n: The print has با (one dot below), a misprint for يا, “O”, corrected here. imraʾat ʿammī, “my uncle’s wife”: ʿAzīz’s mother is ʿAzīza’s aunt by marriage. fī ḥillin min damī, “in release from my blood”: she will not have her death laid on him. wa-lā ākhadhahu, “and may He not hold him to account”: lā with a perfect verb makes a wish. The print sets a madda over the article’s alif in آلاخرة; the word is al-ākhira, “the last (abode)”, the world to come. al-dār al-dunyā, “the nearer abode”, this world. lammā mātat, “when she died”: at her death; she speaks in her last moments.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ يَا بِنْتِي سَلَامَتُكِ وَسَلَامَتُ شَبَابِكِ وَصِرْتُ أَسْأَلُهَا عَنْ سَبَبِ مَرَضِهَا فَمَا تَكَلَّمَتْ ثُمَّ تَبَسَّمَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu yā bintī salāmatuki wa-salāmatu shabābiki wa-ṣirtu asʾaluhā ʿan sababi maraḍihā fa-mā takallamat thumma tabassamat
sentences.l: And I said: O my daughter, your safety and the safety of your youth! And I began asking her about the cause of her illness, and she did not speak; then she smiled
sentences.i: I said, ‘My daughter, may you be well, may your youth be spared!’ And I kept asking her what the cause of her illness was, but she would not speak. Then she smiled
sentences.n: salāmatuki, “your safety”: what one says to the sick, “may you be well”. The print writes salāmat with an open tāʾ (سلامت), a spelling it uses now and then for the closed ة. ṣirtu asʾaluhā, “I became asking her”: ṣāra with a present verb, “began to, kept on”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ يَا امْرَأَةَ عَمِّي قُولِي لِابْنِكِ إِذَا أَرَادَ الرَّوَاحَ إِلَى الْمَوْضِعِ الَّذِي يَرُوحُهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ يَقُولُ هَذَيْنِ الْكَلِمَتَيْنِ عِنْدَ انْصِرَافِهِ مِنْهُ الْوَفَاءُ مَلِيحٌ * وَالْغَدْرُ قَبِيحٌ *
sentences.tr: wa-qālat yā imraʾata ʿammī qūlī li-ibniki idhā arāda al-rawāḥa ilā al-mawḍiʿi alladhī yarūḥuhu kulla yawmin yaqūlu hādhayni al-kalimatayni ʿinda inṣirāfihi minhu al-wafāʾu malīḥun * wa-al-ghadru qabīḥun *
sentences.l: and said: O wife of my uncle, say to your son, when he wants the going to the place which he goes-to every day, he says these two words at his departing from it: Faithfulness (is) fine; * and treachery (is) foul. *
sentences.i: and said, ‘O my aunt, tell your son that when he means to go to the place he goes to every day, he should say these two sayings as he leaves it: Faithfulness is fair, and treachery is foul.
sentences.n: li-ibniki, “to your son”: li- marks the one spoken to, after qūlī, “say”. yaqūlu, “he says”: where Classical would want a command (fal-yaqul, “let him say”), the spoken idiom puts the plain present. hādhayni al-kalimatayni: a masculine “these two” with the feminine kalima, a spoken agreement. The two sayings rhyme, malīḥ and qabīḥ, and the print marks them off with stars.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ هَذِهِ شَفَقَةٌ مِنِّي عَلَيْهِ لِأَكُونَ شَغُوفَةً عَلَيْهِ فِي حَيَاتِي وَبَعْدَ مَمَاتِي
sentences.tr: fa-inna hādhihi shafaqatun minnī ʿalayhi li-akūna shaghūfatan ʿalayhi fī ḥayātī wa-baʿda mamātī
sentences.l: For this (is) a tenderness from me upon him, that I may be devoted over him in my life and after my death.
sentences.i: For this is my care for him, so that I may watch over him with love in my life and after my death.’
sentences.n: shaghūfa ʿalayhi, “passionately caring for him”: shaghūf is love that has reached the heart’s lining (shaghāf); with ʿalā it leans toward anxious care. li-akūna: li- before the verb, “so that I may be”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعْطَتْنِي لَكَ حَاجَةً وَحَلَّفَتْنِي أَنِّي لَا أُعْطِيهَا لَكَ حَتَّى أَرَاكَ تَبْكِي عَلَيْهَا وَتَنُوحُ وَالْحَاجَةُ عِنْدِي فَإِذَا رَأَيْتُكَ عَلَى الصِّفَةِ الَّتِي ذَكَرَتْهَا أَعْطَيْتُكَ إِيَّاهَا
sentences.tr: thumma aʿṭatnī laka ḥājatan wa-ḥallafatnī annī lā uʿṭīhā laka ḥattā arāka tabkī ʿalayhā wa-tanūḥu wa-al-ḥājatu ʿindī fa-idhā raʾaytuka ʿalā al-ṣifati allatī dhakarathā aʿṭaytuka iyyāhā
sentences.l: Then she gave me for you a thing, and made-me-swear that I would not give it to you until I see you weeping over her and lamenting; and the thing (is) with me. So when I see you in the state which she mentioned, I (will) give you it.
sentences.i: Then she gave me something for you, and made me swear not to give it to you until I saw you weeping and mourning for her. I have it here; when I see you as she described, I will give it to you.”
sentences.n: ḥāja, “a thing, an object”: in spoken Arabic the word for “need” is also simply “a thing”. laka, “for you”: li- of the one it is meant for. ḥallafa, “make (someone) swear”. idhā raʾaytuka … aʿṭaytuka: the perfect after idhā, and in the answer, speaks of the future, “when I see you, I will give”.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَرِنِي إِيَّاهَا فَمَا رَضِيَتْ ثُمَّ إِنِّي اشْتَغَلْتُ بِلَذَّاتِي فَمَا ذَكَرْتُ أَنَا مَوْتَ ابْنَةِ عَمِّي لِأَنِّي كُنْتُ طَائِشَ الْعَقْلِ وَكُنْتُ أَوَدُّ فِي نَفْسِي أَنْ أَكُونَ طُولَ لَيْلِي وَنَهَارِي عِنْدَ مَحْبُوبَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā arinī iyyāhā fa-mā raḍiyat thumma innī ishtaghaltu bi-ladhdhātī fa-mā dhakartu anā mawta ibnati ʿammī li-annī kuntu ṭāʾisha al-ʿaqli wa-kuntu awaddu fī nafsī an akūna ṭūla laylī wa-nahārī ʿinda maḥbūbatī
sentences.l: And I said to her: Show-me it; and she was not willing. Then I busied myself with my pleasures, and I did not remember, I, the death of the daughter of my uncle, because I was flighty of the mind; and I used to wish in myself that I be the length of my night and my day with my beloved.
sentences.i: I said to her, “Show it to me,” but she would not. Then I gave myself up to my pleasures and gave no thought to my cousin’s death, for my wits were giddy, and all I wished was to be with my beloved all night and all day.
sentences.n: arinī, “show me”: the print has the masculine imperative (ارني), though he is speaking to his mother; the feminine would be arīnī. Spoken Arabic often lets the masculine stand. ishtaghala bi-, “busy oneself with”: the verb chooses the bi-. ṭāʾish al-ʿaqli, “light of mind, reckless”.

sentences.t: وَمَاصَدَّقْتُ أَنَّ اللَّيْلَ أَقْبَلَ حَتَّى مَضَيْتُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ فَوَجَدْتُ الصَّبِيَّةَ جَالِسَةً عَلَى مَقَالِى النَّارِ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الِانْتِظَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā ṣaddaqtu anna al-layla aqbala ḥattā maḍaytu ilā al-bustāni fa-wajadtu al-ṣabiyyata jālisatan ʿalā maqālī al-nāri min kathrati al-intiẓāri
sentences.l: And I did not believe that the night had come, until I went-off to the garden; and I found the girl sitting upon frying-pans of the fire from the much of the waiting.
sentences.i: Night had hardly come before I was off to the garden, and I found the young woman sitting as if on hot coals from waiting so long.
sentences.n: mā ṣaddaqtu anna … ḥattā, “I did not believe that … until”: a spoken idiom for “no sooner … than”, the thing longed for comes and one goes at once. ʿalā maqālī al-nār, “on frying pans over the fire”: on hot coals. The print runs وما and صدقت together, and spells maqālī with a final ى.

sentences.t: فَمَا صَدَّقَتْ أَنَّهَا رَأَتْنِي وَتَعَلَّقَتْ بِي وَبَادَرَتْ إِلَى رَقَبَتِي وَسَأَلَتْنِي عَنْ بِنْتِ عَمِّي فَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِنَّهَا مَاتَتْ وَعَمِلْنَا لَهَا الذِّكْرَ وَالْخُتُومَ وَمَضَى لَهَا أَرْبَعُ لَيَالٍ وَهَذِهِ الْخَامِسَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā ṣaddaqat annahā raʾatnī wa-taʿallaqat bī wa-bādarat ilā raqabatī wa-saʾalatnī ʿan binti ʿammī fa-qultu lahā innahā mātat wa-ʿamilnā lahā al-dhikra wa-al-khutūma wa-maḍā lahā arbaʿu layālin wa-hādhihi al-khāmisatu
sentences.l: And she did not believe that she saw me, and she clung to me and rushed to my neck, and asked me about the daughter of my uncle. And I said to her: She died, and we made for her the remembrance and the complete-recitations, and four nights have passed for her, and this (is) the fifth.
sentences.i: She could hardly believe she was seeing me; she clung to me and threw her arms round my neck, and asked me about my cousin. I told her, “She is dead. We have had the prayers and the readings of the Qurʾān made for her; four nights have gone by since, and this is the fifth.”
sentences.n: fa-mā ṣaddaqat annahā raʾatnī, “she did not believe she saw me”: the same idiom again, from her side. taʿallaqa bi-, “cling to”: the verb chooses the bi-. al-dhikr, “the remembrance”, chanting God’s names for the dead; al-khutūm, another plural of khatma, the full readings of the Qurʾān. The print spells raʾatnī and saʾalatnī without the hamza, راتني and سالتني.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ ذَلِكَ صَاحَتْ وَبَكَتْ وَقَالَتْ أَمَا قُلْتُ لَكَ إِنَّكَ قَتَلْتَهَا وَلَوْ أَعْلَمْتَنِي بِهَا قَبْلَ مَوْتِهَا لَكُنْتُ أُكَافِئُهَا عَلَى مَافَعَلَتْ مَعِي مِنَ الْمَعْرُوفِ فَإِنَّهَا خَدَمَتْنِي وَأَوْصَلَتْكَ إِلَيَّ وَلَوْلَاهَا مَا اجْتَمَعْتُ أَنَا وَإِيَّاكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat dhālika ṣāḥat wa-bakat wa-qālat a-mā qultu laka innaka qataltahā wa-law aʿlamtanī bihā qabla mawtihā la-kuntu ukāfiʾuhā ʿalā mā faʿalat maʿī mina al-maʿrūfi fa-innahā khadamatnī wa-awṣalatka ilayya wa-lawlāhā mā ijtamaʿtu anā wa-iyyāka
sentences.l: And when she heard that, she cried-out and wept and said: Did I not say to you that you killed her? And if you had informed me about her before her death, I would have been repaying her for what she did with me of the kindness; for she served me and brought-you-through to me, and but for her I would not have come-together, I and you.
sentences.i: When she heard this she cried out and wept and said, “Did I not tell you that you had killed her? If only you had told me about her before she died, I would have repaid her for the kindness she did me. She served me and brought you to me; but for her, you and I would never have come together.”
sentences.n: a-mā, “did … not?”: a- asks the question, mā denies. aʿlama bi-, “inform of”: the verb chooses the bi-. la-kuntu ukāfiʾuhā, “I would have been repaying her”: la- opens the answer to law, “if”. min al-maʿrūf, “of kindness”: min names what it was she did. The print runs ما and فعلت together.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا خَائِفَةٌ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَقَعَ بِكَ رَزِيَّةٌ بِسَبَبِ خَطِيئَتِهَا فَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِنَّهَا قَدْ جَعَلَتْنِي فِي حِلٍّ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهَا ثُمَّ ذَكَرْتُ لَهَا مَا أَخْبَرَتْنِي بِهِ أُمِّي
sentences.tr: wa-anā khāʾifatun ʿalayka an taqaʿa bika raziyyatun bi-sababi khaṭīʾatihā fa-qultu lahā innahā qad jaʿalatnī fī ḥillin qabla mawtihā thumma dhakartu lahā mā akhbaratnī bihi ummī
sentences.l: And I (am) fearful for you that a calamity befall on you because of the sin of her. And I said to her: She (has) made me in release before her death. Then I mentioned to her what my mother informed me of.
sentences.i: “And I fear for you, that some calamity will fall on you because of the wrong done to her.” I told her, “She released me from it before she died,” and then I told her what my mother had told me.
sentences.n: waqaʿa bi-, “befall, fall upon”: bi- marks the one it falls on. khaṭīʾatuhā, “her sin”: the sin against her, the guilt of her death, as at the night’s opening. akhbara bi-, “inform of”: the verb chooses the bi-; bihi, “of it”, refers back to mā, “what”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ إِذَا ذَهَبْتَ إِلَى أُمِّكَ فَاعْرِفِ الْحَاجَةَ الَّتِي عِنْدَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat bi-allāhi ʿalayka idhā dhahabta ilā ummika fa-iʿrifi al-ḥājata allatī ʿindahā
sentences.l: And she said: By God upon you, when you go to your mother, then know the thing which (is) with her.
sentences.i: She said, “I beg you by God, when you go to your mother, find out what the thing is that she has.”
sentences.n: bi-allāhi ʿalayka, “by God upon you”: bi- of the oath; the formula of an earnest plea. fa-iʿrif, “then find out”: fa- opens the answer to idhā.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِنَّ أُمِّي قَالَتْ لِي إِنَّ ابْنَةَ عَمِّكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَمُوتَ أَوْصَتْنِي وَقَالَتْ لِي إِذَا أَرَادَ ابْنُكِ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ إِلَى الْمَوْضِعِ الَّذِي عَادَتُهُ الذَّهَابُ إِلَيْهِ فَقُولِي لَهُ هَاتَيْنِ الْكَلِمَتَيْنِ الْوَفَاءُ مَلِيحٌ * وَالْغَدْرُ قَبِيحٌ *
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā inna ummī qālat lī inna ibnata ʿammika qabla an tamūta awṣatnī wa-qālat lī idhā arāda ibnuki an yadhhaba ilā al-mawḍiʿi alladhī ʿādatuhu al-dhahābu ilayhi fa-qūlī lahu hātayni al-kalimatayni al-wafāʾu malīḥun * wa-al-ghadru qabīḥun *
sentences.l: And I said to her: My mother said to me: The daughter of your uncle, before she died, charged me and said to me: When your son wants to go to the place which his habit (is) the going to it, then say to him these two words: Faithfulness (is) fine; * and treachery (is) foul. *
sentences.i: I said to her, “My mother told me that before my cousin died she gave her a charge, and said to her, ‘When your son means to go to the place he goes to by habit, tell him these two sayings: Faithfulness is fair, and treachery is foul.’”
sentences.n: alladhī ʿādatuhu al-dhahābu ilayhi, “which his habit is the going to it”: the place he is in the habit of going to. hātayni al-kalimatayni: here the feminine “these two” agrees with kalima, as it did not when the mother first reported the words.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ ذَلِكَ قَالَتْ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهَا فَإِنَّهَا خَلَّصَتْكَ مِنِّي وَقَدْ كُنْتُ أَضْمَرْتُ عَلَى ضَرَرِكَ فَأَنَا لَا أَضُرُّكَ وَلَا أُشَوِّشُ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-ṣabiyyatu dhālika qālat raḥmatu allāhi taʿālā ʿalayhā fa-innahā khallaṣatka minnī wa-qad kuntu aḍmartu ʿalā ḍararika fa-anā lā aḍurruka wa-lā ushawwishu ʿalayka
sentences.l: And when the girl heard that, she said: The mercy of God, exalted (is) He, (be) upon her! For she (has) delivered you from me; and I had resolved-secretly upon your harm. So I (will) not harm you and not trouble upon you.
sentences.i: When the young woman heard this she said, “God’s mercy be on her! She has saved you from me. I had secretly meant to do you harm; now I will not harm you or trouble you.”
sentences.n: aḍmara ʿalā, “hide in the heart, secretly intend”: with ʿalā, a purpose aimed against someone. shawwasha ʿalā, “trouble, upset”: a spoken verb, from the same root as mutashawwish, “troubled”.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبْتُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَمَاكُنْتِ تُرِيدِينَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ أَنْ تَفْعَلِيهِ مَعِي وَقَدْ صَارَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكِ مَوَدَّةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjabtu min dhālika wa-qultu lahā wa-mā kunti turīdīna qabla dhālika an tafʿalīhi maʿī wa-qad ṣāra baynī wa-baynaki mawaddatun
sentences.l: And I marvelled at that and said to her: And what were you wanting before that, that you do it with me, when there had become between me and between you affection?
sentences.i: I was astonished at this and said to her, “And what did you mean to do to me before, when there was love between you and me?”
sentences.n: wa-qad ṣāra, “when there had come to be”: wa- with qad and a verb sets a circumstance, here a protest, “even though”. ṣāra is masculine before the feminine mawadda, as often when the verb comes first. The print runs وما and كنت together.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أَنْتَ مُولَعٌ بِي وَلَكِنَّكَ صَغِيرُ السِّنِّ وَغَشِيمٌ وَقَلْبُكَ خَالٍ عَنِ الْخِدَاعِ فَأَنْتَ لَا تَعْرِفُ مَكْرَنَا وَلَاخِدَاعَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat anta mūlaʿun bī wa-lākinnaka ṣaghīru al-sinni wa-ghashīmun wa-qalbuka khālin ʿani al-khidāʿi fa-anta lā taʿrifu makranā wa-lā khidāʿanā
sentences.l: And she said: You (are) infatuated with me, but you (are) small of the age and raw, and your heart (is) empty of the deceiving; so you do not know our cunning and not our deceiving.
sentences.i: She said, “You are mad for me, but you are young and green, and your heart knows nothing of deceit, so you do not know our cunning or our wiles.
sentences.n: The print has والمنك, a misprint for ولكنك (wa-lākinnaka, “but you”), corrected here. mūlaʿ bi-, “infatuated with”: the word chooses the bi-. ghashīm, “raw, inexperienced”: a spoken word. The print runs ولا and خداعنا together.

sentences.t: وَلَوْ كَانَتْ عَاشَتْ لَكَانَتْ مُعِينَةً لَكَ فَإِنَّهَا سَبَبُ سَلَامَتِكَ وَكَانَتْ أَنْجَتْكَ مِنَ الْمَهْلَكَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-law kānat ʿāshat la-kānat muʿīnatan laka fa-innahā sababu salāmatika wa-kānat anjatka mina al-mahlakati
sentences.l: And if she had lived, she would have been a helper to you; for she (is) the cause of your safety, and she had rescued you from the perdition.
sentences.i: Had she lived, she would have been your helper; she is the reason you are safe, and she saved you from ruin.
sentences.n: law kānat ʿāshat, “if she had lived”: kāna with a perfect verb sets the condition further in the past. la-kānat: la- opens the answer to law.

sentences.t: وَالْآنَ أُوصِيكَ أَنْ لَا تَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَ وَاحِدَةٍ وَلَا تُخَاطِبَ وَاحِدَةً مِنْ أَمْثَالِنَا لَاصَغِيرَةً وَلَا كَبِيرَةً فَإِيَّاكَ ثُمَّ إِيَّاكَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-āna ūṣīka an lā tatakallama maʿa wāḥidatin wa-lā tukhāṭiba wāḥidatan min amthālinā lā ṣaghīratan wa-lā kabīratan fa-iyyāka thumma iyyāka
sentences.l: And now I charge you that you not speak with one (woman) and not address one of our likes, not small and not great; so beware, then beware!
sentences.i: And now I charge you: speak to no woman, and have no words with any of our kind, young or old. Beware, I tell you, beware!
sentences.n: min amthālinā, “of our likes”: women like her. iyyāka, “beware”: the bare pronoun “you” used as a warning, “(keep) yourself (away)!”; doubled for weight. The print runs لا and صغيرة together, and puts a shadda on ايّاك.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّكَ غَشِيمٌ وَغَيْرُ عَارِفٍ بِخِدَاعِ النِّسَاءِ وَمَكْرِهِنَّ وَالَّتِي كَانَتْ تُفَسِّرُ لَكَ الْإِشَارَاتِ قَدْ مَاتَتْ وَإِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي رَزِيَّةٍ فَمَا تَلْقَى مَنْ يُخَلِّصُكَ مِنْهَا بَعْدَ مَوْتِ بِنْتِ عَمِّكَ
sentences.tr: fa-innaka ghashīmun wa-ghayru ʿārifin bi-khidāʿi al-nisāʾi wa-makrihinna wa-allatī kānat tufassiru laka al-ishārāti qad mātat wa-innī akhāfu ʿalayka an taqaʿa fī raziyyatin fa-mā talqā man yukhalliṣuka minhā baʿda mawti binti ʿammika
sentences.l: For you (are) raw and not knowing of the deceiving of the women and their cunning; and she who used to explain to you the signs (has) died; and I fear for you that you fall into a calamity, and you (will) not find who (will) deliver you from it after the death of the daughter of your uncle.
sentences.i: You are green, and know nothing of women’s deceit and their cunning; and she who used to explain the signs to you is dead. I fear you will fall into some calamity, and there will be no one to get you out of it, now that your cousin is dead.”
sentences.n: ʿārif bi-, “knowing about, versed in”: the word chooses the bi-. al-ishārāt, “the signs”: the riddling gestures the lady made at their first meetings, which ʿAzīza read for him.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
